title: Catena app declaration block
description: The x-catena block at the top level of blueprints/<id>/docker-compose.yml: what the host needs to update, back up and restore the deployed app without reading the catalog. Portainer stores the compose byte for byte, so the block travels with the app. catena-admin payload/engines/appdecl reads it. A block holds no $ (Docker interpolates it when it deploys the file), except in a hooks script body where each $ is written $$, and names no image of its file (an update rewrites those).

lifecycle.description: Commands the host runs inside one service around a schema change, and volumes it copies around an update of that service: the commands around every image update the update lane applies, the migration only when the update moves that service's image, and after a FORWARD restore once the database replay has put the snapshot's contents back. Declare it when the application keeps a schema its new code expects migrated (migrate), or when its new version upgrades state in a volume that the previous version then refuses or misreads (versioned_volumes); an entry declares one or both. A migration the application runs at container start is not enough on a restore: it runs against the pre-replay database and the replay then overwrites it. Every command is an argv array executed through docker exec, never a shell.

service.description: Compose service the commands run inside, and whose new version upgrades the versioned volumes.

user.description: User to exec as. Set it whenever a command writes into a volume the application later has to write itself, or the files come back owned by root.

migrate.description: The schema migration. Run in order, stopping at the first failure; a failure after an update rolls the image AND the database back.

before_update.description: Run in the RUNNING container just before the update lane deploys the new image (put the application into maintenance mode).

after_update.description: Run once the update settles, whether it was kept or rolled back (take the application out of maintenance mode).

ready.description: A command that exits 0 once the application can run the commands above. Before each phase of an update, the update lane runs it every few seconds until it succeeds, for up to timeout_seconds. Every lifecycle block declares it: the container runs from the moment the entrypoint starts, and every command fails until an entrypoint that copies or upgrades the application is done. It has to succeed in the state before_update leaves the application in. make lint requires it.

versioned_volumes.description: Named volumes the new version of the service upgrades in place and the previous version refuses to start on or misreads: the application's code tree, its configuration, its add-ons, or the database files it keeps in a volume (SQLite). The update lane copies each one before an update that moves the service, with the application in its backup mode when it declares one, and, when the update rolls back, puts the copy back with every service that mounts it stopped; what was written to the volume since the copy is lost, as a database dump's replay loses it. A volume of the users' files that the previous version still reads stays out, and so does one a database or a one-shot service mounts: a rollback does not stop either.

timeout_seconds.description: Ceiling for each command, database dump and replay, and volume copy and put-back.

quiesce.description: Commands the nightly maintenance runs inside one service around its backup, for an application whose live state a file-level snapshot can tear and the backup's own database dumps do not cover. Every command is an argv array executed through docker exec, never a shell. post must succeed when pre never ran: it runs after every backup attempt, after a resumed run and after a restore.

service.description: Compose service the commands run inside.

user.description: User to exec as, when the application refuses to run its CLI as root.

pre.description: Run in order before the backup, stopping at the first failure.

post.description: Run in order after the backup, whether it succeeded or not, stopping at the first failure.

s3_reconcile.description: Post-restore object-store consistency check. Report-only: it names the orphan rows, it never deletes them, because a bucket that is misconfigured looks exactly like a bucket that is empty.

service.description: Compose service the check runs inside.

user.description: User to exec as, when the app refuses to run its CLI as root.

db_service.description: Compose service holding the index the check reads.

object_store.description: How the app reaches its object-store bucket, for the host to point a deployed app at another bucket. env names the stack env keys that hold the bucket's settings. switch is what the host runs once the app runs on the new bucket; its commands may carry the placeholders {old_bucket} and {new_bucket}.

env.description: Stack env key of each setting. host, port, ssl and region are named when the template exposes them.

switch.description: Commands run inside one service after the app runs on the new bucket. Every command is an argv array executed through docker exec, never a shell.

service.description: Compose service the commands run inside.

user.description: User to exec as, when the application refuses to run its CLI as root.

commands.description: Run in order, stopping at the first failure.

setting.description: A value a person may change. default is its first value; the deploy form shows label when the setting has one and a name made from the key otherwise.

generated.description: A secret the host mints on the first deploy: length characters of alphabet.

managed.description: A key the host's dashboard-sync re-injects into a running stack whenever it drifts from what the panel renders (a rotated credential, a changed domain), with the expression its value is rendered from. In the public catalog it renders to the operator-wired sentinel, never to a real value.

env.description: The application's environment, in the order the deploy form shows it. Each key is exactly one of a setting, a generated secret or a managed expression.

version_from.description: The service whose image tag is the application's version. Empty is the main address's service. It names a service of the file.

hooks.description: Scripts the host runs inside one service: configure after a deploy, verify that the application works, users to seed its accounts. Each body is a list of argv; a $ in one is written $$, which Docker reads back as $.

users_group.description: The path of the realm group (staff, or staff/sales) whose members, with those of its subgroups, the users hook receives on its standard input as a JSON list when they change. Several paths are separated by commas.

needs.description: What the application needs of the host: a certificate written into one of its volumes, and DNS records in its zone. A name or a value may hold {{ name }} expressions, which read the keys of the application's .env (lowercased) and the host's facts such as public_ip.

data.description: Per service, the volume it keeps its data in and how that data upgrades: a dump replayed after the update, or in place.

write_hold.description: What holds the application's writers still while a backup or an update runs. Absent, the host derives it.

rule.description: How the tags of the image read as versions (catena-admin payload/engines/tagrule). A tag_pattern is matched against the whole tag, so it carries no anchors, and a block holds no $.

images.description: Per service, the bump policy of its image and the rule that reads its tags.

secrets.description: The store secrets the managed expressions may read.

stops.description: Application versions an update must pass through.

privileges.description: The host privileges the application asks for.

host_paths.description: The host folders and files outside its own data folder (/srv/catena/apps/<stack>) that the application binds, each an absolute path. A bind inside one passes the app checker (X17). The Docker socket and the compose folders stay refused whatever is declared.

provides.description: The capabilities the application offers, each value the name of a key of env. Another application reads them in a managed expression as provided.<capability>.<name>.
